title: Toy joy!
paragraphs: I’m sure we all have childhood memories – what we did at school, the food we ate, the games we played. But perhaps the most vivid recollections are those of the toys we played with. There were many gadgets that may seem unsophisticated now but were the must-have items in the playground back in the day. Now it seems that our passion for nostalgia means some of them are making a comeback.

One of my favourites was the Nintendo Game Boy, which returned to the shops last year, 30 years after it was first released. This handheld console has had some modifications, but still offers a simple gaming experience and a trip down memory lane! If the Game Boy wasn’t from your era, how about the Tamagotchi? This egg-shaped, plastic pet that its owner had to keep ‘alive’ with constant care and attention - was the must-have item not long after its launch in 1996.

These sometimes annoying ‘creatures’ were such a distraction in the classroom, they often got banned from school. But now, childlike adults can relive their wasted youth because Japanese manufacturer Bandai will soon release an all-colour, new-and-improved version of the classic toy. Its maker says it’s evolved from a pet into more of a character, and can inhabit different lands, as well as get married and breed.

So what’s driving this demand for retro goods? Retail Analyst for Mintel, Chana Baram, told the BBC people are searching for comfort in 'the good old days'. Certainly, playing with an old toy brings back memories of our formative years and gives us a feel-good factor, but it’s also something brands and marketing companies want to cash in on.

Retro toys are also something we could cash in on too. In the darkest corners of many attics and spare rooms lie the toys of Christmas past. And those once much-loved and played with presents may now have a value beyond nostalgia. Toyologist Peter Jenkinson told the BBC that any number of "toys that we all played with as kids are now worth more than a few quid". He suggests there’s a real collectors' market for certain old board games, Star Wars characters, Sindy dolls and Lego sets. However, if you own something like this, it may be just too precious to sell, and part with the connection to your childhood.

vocabulary.entry: vivid recollection /ˈvɪvɪd ˌrekəˈlekʃn/ 清晰的回忆；鲜活的记忆
vocabulary.example: The smell of the sea brought back vivid recollections of her childhood holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 大海的气息唤起了她对童年假期的清晰回忆。

vocabulary.entry: unsophisticated /ˌʌnsəˈfɪstɪkeɪtɪd/ adj. 简陋的；不复杂的
vocabulary.example: The unsophisticated machine still works well after so many years.
vocabulary.translation: 这台简陋的机器过了这么多年依然运转良好。

vocabulary.entry: must-have item /ˈmʌst hæv ˈaɪtəm/ 必备单品；热门商品
vocabulary.example: This type of jacket was a must-have item among teenagers last winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这款夹克去年冬天是青少年人手必备的单品。

vocabulary.entry: nostalgia /nɒˈstældʒə/ n. 怀旧；怀旧情怀
vocabulary.example: The old film filled her with nostalgia for her hometown.
vocabulary.translation: 这部老电影让她对故乡充满了怀旧之情。

vocabulary.entry: make a comeback /meɪk ə ˈkʌmbæk/ 再度流行；卷土重来
vocabulary.example: Bell-bottom trousers have made a comeback in recent fashion shows.
vocabulary.translation: 喇叭裤在最近的时装秀上再度流行起来。

vocabulary.entry: handheld console /ˈhændheld ˈkɒnsəʊl/ 掌上游戏机
vocabulary.example: He spent the whole journey playing games on his handheld console.
vocabulary.translation: 他整个旅途都在玩掌上游戏机。

vocabulary.entry: modification /ˌmɒdɪfɪˈkeɪʃn/ n. 修改；改良
vocabulary.example: The design of the car has undergone several modifications.
vocabulary.translation: 这款汽车的设计已经过数次改良。

vocabulary.entry: a trip down memory lane /ə trɪp daʊn ˈmeməri leɪn/ 重温回忆；回忆往事
vocabulary.example: Looking at old photos is a nice trip down memory lane.
vocabulary.translation: 翻看旧照片是一段很惬意的回忆往事的时光。

vocabulary.entry: launch /lɔːntʃ/ v. 推出（产品）；上市
vocabulary.example: The company plans to launch a new smartphone next month.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司计划下个月推出一款新智能手机。

vocabulary.entry: distraction /dɪˈstrækʃn/ n. 分心的事物；干扰
vocabulary.example: The noise outside was a distraction to the students in the classroom.
vocabulary.translation: 外面的噪音干扰了教室里的学生。

vocabulary.entry: relive /ˌriːˈlɪv/ v. 重温；再体验
vocabulary.example: She likes to relive the happy moments of her wedding day.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢重温婚礼当天的幸福时刻。

vocabulary.entry: evolve /ɪˈvɒlv/ v. 演变；进化
vocabulary.example: The simple game has evolved into a popular online sport.
vocabulary.translation: 这款简单的游戏已经演变成了一项热门的线上运动。

vocabulary.entry: inhabit /ɪnˈhæbɪt/ v. 居住于；栖息在
vocabulary.example: Many rare birds inhabit the wetland in spring and autumn.
vocabulary.translation: 春秋两季，许多珍稀鸟类栖息在这片湿地。

vocabulary.entry: breed /briːd/ v. 繁殖；生育
vocabulary.example: These animals breed in the warmer months of the year.
vocabulary.translation: 这些动物在一年中气候较温暖的月份繁殖。

vocabulary.entry: retro goods /ˈretrə ɡʊdz/ 复古商品
vocabulary.example: The shop specializes in selling retro goods from the 1980s.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店专门售卖20世纪80年代的复古商品。

vocabulary.entry: formative years /ˈfɔːmətɪv jɪəz/ 成长时期；性格形成时期
vocabulary.example: Her formative years were spent in a small village by the sea.
vocabulary.translation: 她的成长时期是在海边的一个小村庄度过的。

vocabulary.entry: feel-good factor /ˈfiːl ɡʊd ˈfæktə(r)/ 愉悦感；幸福感
vocabulary.example: The music festival has a great feel-good factor for everyone who attends.
vocabulary.translation: 这场音乐节给所有参与者都带来了强烈的愉悦感。

vocabulary.entry: cash in on /kæʃ ɪn ɒn/ 从……中牟利；利用
vocabulary.example: Some companies are trying to cash in on the public's interest in healthy food.
vocabulary.translation: 一些公司正试图利用公众对健康食品的兴趣来牟利。

vocabulary.entry: attic /ˈætɪk/ n. 阁楼
vocabulary.example: They found a box of old letters in the attic of the house.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在房子的阁楼里发现了一箱旧信件。

vocabulary.entry: quid /kwɪd/ n. 英镑（英国口语）
vocabulary.example: The book cost me only a few quid at the second-hand shop.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书我在二手书店只花了几英镑。

vocabulary.entry: collectors' market /kəˈlektəz ˈmɑːkɪt/ 收藏市场
vocabulary.example: There is a growing collectors' market for vintage vinyl records.
vocabulary.translation: 复古黑胶唱片的收藏市场正在不断扩大。

vocabulary.entry: part with /pɑːt wɪð/ 舍弃；放弃
vocabulary.example: She couldn't bear to part with her childhood teddy bear.
vocabulary.translation: 她舍不得舍弃自己童年的泰迪熊玩偶。

sentences.english: I’m sure we all have childhood memories – what we did at school, the food we ate, the games we played.
sentences.chinese: 我相信每个人都有属于自己的童年回忆——上学时的趣事、吃过的美食、玩过的游戏。

sentences.english: But perhaps the most vivid recollections are those of the toys we played with.
sentences.chinese: 但或许最鲜活的记忆，是那些陪伴我们成长的玩具。

sentences.english: There were many gadgets that may seem unsophisticated now but were the must-have items in the playground back in the day.
sentences.chinese: 有许多小玩意儿如今看来可能显得简陋，但在当年的操场上，它们可是人手必备的热门单品。

sentences.english: Now it seems that our passion for nostalgia means some of them are making a comeback.
sentences.chinese: 而现在，人们对怀旧情怀的热衷，让其中一些玩具正重新流行起来。

sentences.english: One of my favourites was the Nintendo Game Boy, which returned to the shops last year, 30 years after it was first released.
sentences.chinese: 我最喜欢的玩具之一就是任天堂的Game Boy掌上游戏机。这款产品在发布30年后，于去年重返市场。

sentences.english: This handheld console has had some modifications, but still offers a simple gaming experience and a trip down memory lane!
sentences.chinese: 它的掌机外观做了些许改良，但依旧能带来简单纯粹的游戏体验，让人重温往昔时光！

sentences.english: If the Game Boy wasn’t from your era, how about the Tamagotchi?
sentences.chinese: 如果Game Boy不属于你的童年时代，那电子宠物鸡呢？

sentences.english: This egg-shaped, plastic pet that its owner had to keep ‘alive’ with constant care and attention - was the must-have item not long after its launch in 1996.
sentences.chinese: 这款鸡蛋形状的塑料宠物玩具需要玩家必须悉心照料才能让它“存活”下去，于1996年推出后不久就成了爆款。

sentences.english: These sometimes annoying ‘creatures’ were such a distraction in the classroom, they often got banned from school.
sentences.chinese: 这些有时会惹人烦的“小家伙”在教室分散学生们的注意力，因此常常被学校禁止带入。

sentences.english: But now, childlike adults can relive their wasted youth because Japanese manufacturer Bandai will soon release an all-colour, new-and-improved version of the classic toy.
sentences.chinese: 但如今，童心未泯的成年人可以重拾逝去的青春了——日本制造商万代即将推出这款经典玩具的全新彩色升级版。

sentences.english: Its maker says it’s evolved from a pet into more of a character, and can inhabit different lands, as well as get married and breed.
sentences.chinese: 制造商表示，新款电子宠物鸡不再只是一个宠物，更像是一个角色，它可以居住在不同的场景中，还能结婚生子。

sentences.english: So what’s driving this demand for retro goods?
sentences.chinese: 那么，是什么催生了人们对复古商品的需求呢？

sentences.english: Retail Analyst for Mintel, Chana Baram, told the BBC people are searching for comfort in 'the good old days'.
sentences.chinese: 英敏特零售分析师钱娜·巴拉姆向英国广播公司表示，人们正从“往昔的美好时光”中寻求慰藉。

sentences.english: Certainly, playing with an old toy brings back memories of our formative years and gives us a feel-good factor, but it’s also something brands and marketing companies want to cash in on.
sentences.chinese: 诚然，把玩旧玩具能唤起我们成长时期的回忆，带来愉悦的心情，但这也是各大品牌和营销公司想要从中牟利的商机。

sentences.english: Retro toys are also something we could cash in on too.
sentences.chinese: 我们普通人也可以从复古玩具中获益。

sentences.english: In the darkest corners of many attics and spare rooms lie the toys of Christmas past.
sentences.chinese: 许多家庭的阁楼和闲置房间的角落里，都藏着当年圣诞节收到的玩具。

sentences.english: And those once much-loved and played with presents may now have a value beyond nostalgia.
sentences.chinese: 这些曾经备受喜爱的礼物，如今的价值或许早已超越了怀旧本身。

sentences.english: Toyologist Peter Jenkinson told the BBC that any number of "toys that we all played with as kids are now worth more than a few quid".
sentences.chinese: 玩具专家彼得·詹金森向英国广播公司透露，“我们小时候玩过的很多玩具，现在都价值不菲”。

sentences.english: He suggests there’s a real collectors' market for certain old board games, Star Wars characters, Sindy dolls and Lego sets.
sentences.chinese: 他指出，一些老式棋盘游戏、星球大战人物模型、仙蒂娃娃和乐高套装，在收藏市场上十分走俏。

sentences.english: However, if you own something like this, it may be just too precious to sell, and part with the connection to your childhood.
sentences.chinese: 不过，如果你也珍藏着这样的玩具，它或许会因为承载着童年的回忆而太过珍贵，让你舍不得出售，不愿割舍这份与童年的联结。
